newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Rare Aug jet fuel export seen to U.S. West Coast.
newsitem.headline: Rare Aug jet fuel export seen to U.S. West Coast.

text.p: In an unexpected move for this time of the year, jet fuel was exported from Asia to the U.S. West Coast, industry sources said on Friday.
A source said that the 30,000-tonne South Korean jet fuel cargo was for lifting during late August for shipment to the U.S. West Coast.

Traders said it was rare for Asia to export jet fuel to the U.S. at this time of the year as the region is a big consumer ahead of the winter season. On the other hand, the U.S. normally exports jet fuel to this region.
Other industry players said the West Coast market is currently the highest priced in the world and many traders are looking to move products to that area.
Talk of further exports from South Korea to either the West Coast or Hawaii was not confirmed.

The price of jet fuel to the West Coast is now above $31 per barrel cost-and-freight (c-and-f) basis while offers from South Korea are below $1.00 per barrel premium to Singapore spot quotes, free-on-board (fob) basis, one trader said.
Traders said that based on freight of about $2.00 per barrel, the arbitrage to the U.S. West Coast is open.
Sources said surplus Caribbean and U.S. Gulf Coast jet fuel supplies have already been shipped to the U.S. West coast.
